summary.intent: Execute Phase 35 (Phala Testnet TEE Migration) end-to-end: restructure TEE worker into monorepo, integrate Phala SDK, deploy CVM to Phala Cloud, and ship the PR.
summary.outcome: All 6 plans across 4 waves executed successfully, CVM deployed and verified on Phala Cloud production infra, security review completed with all H/M findings fixed, PR #395 created and lint passing.

repo: Phase 35 branch is 'phase-35-phala-testnet-tee-migration' — the name is a misnomer; Phala Cloud has no separate testnet, the free tier runs on the same production nodes (Intel TDX hardware, dstack-pha-prod5)

TEE worker was relocated from root tee-worker/ to apps/tee-worker/ and now uses shared monorepo packages: @cipherbox/crypto (ECIES), @cipherbox/core (IPNS signing), @cipherbox/sdk-core (KuboProvider/PsaProvider)

Staging deploy workflow (deploy-staging.yml) has build-tee and deploy-tee-phala jobs triggered by staging-v* tags; both PHALA_CLOUD_API_KEY and STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET are injected at deploy time via GitHub staging environment secrets
ROADMAP.md and STATE.md are the two files most likely to have merge conflicts when merging main into a long-running phase branch
multiformats package (CID.parse) is already a dependency in @cipherbox/crypto and should be used for CID validation instead of hand-rolled regex; tee-worker needed it added as a direct dependency
The entire/* branch stores full conversation transcripts via automatic checkpointing — any secret pasted in conversation will appear in pushed transcripts

PHALA_CLOUD_API_KEY and STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET were exposed in git history (HANDOFF.json commits 607c50fec, bd265fa4f) and in entire branch transcript 86/0546ed796e/0/full.jsonl — both rotated on 2026-03-29

code.finding: Originally called getKeypair() instead of getPublicKey(), leaking private key into route scope — fixed to use getPublicKey()
Was reading TEE_EPOCH env var but migrate route uses TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH — inconsistency fixed to use TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH
Missing MAX_BATCH_SIZE=100 limit — without it, endpoint allowed unbounded ECIES decryption; dead keyEpoch field removed; redundant successes/failures counters replaced with derived values

TOCTOU DNS rebinding vulnerability — DNS lookup was separate from HTTP fetch. Fixed by merging validateResolvedIp into ssrfSafeFetch with DNS pinning: resolve once, connect directly to IP with Host header override. Headers API lowercases keys, so 'host' must be lowercase in constructed headers object.

req.path used as Prometheus label on 404s causes unbounded label cardinality — fixed with '/:unmatched' fallback. PR review caught that label should be '/:unmatched' not 'unmatched' to match Express route convention.

Was reading TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH at module load (stale after rotation); fixed to accept currentEpoch from request body with env var fallback. CID validation uses CID.parse() from multiformats, not hand-rolled regex.
After DNS pinning was added to ssrfSafeFetch, tests needed dns/promises mocked for non-simulator mode. Two new DNS pinning tests added, total test count went from 56 to 58.

workflow: GSD worktree agents can cause git config lock contention when run in parallel — running Wave 2 agents sequentially after the first parallel attempt failed avoided this
classifyHandoffIfNeeded is a known Claude Code runtime bug — agents report 'failed' but spot-checks (SUMMARY.md + commits present) confirm actual success
pause-work / resume-work handoff cycle works across machines: push branch, pull on new host, /gsd:resume-work restores full context including credentials from HANDOFF.json
Secrets in HANDOFF.json committed to git are exposed — rotate immediately after session that required them; the entire branch transcript system also captures conversation-level secrets
Security review should be run before shipping any crypto-adjacent phase; the /security:review command generates .planning/security/REVIEW-*.md with severity-tagged findings

friction: Wave 2 parallel agent execution failed initially due to git config lock contention between concurrent worktree agents — had to fall back to sequential
Usage limit hit mid-session during Wave 2 execution, requiring manual 'continue please' to resume
gsd-tools init runs from CWD — when invoked from the main repo root rather than the worktree, phase_found returns false; had to re-run from worktree path
Docker not available locally (runs on 192.168.133.12) — required session transfer via pause-work/resume-work to build and push the TEE worker image
PHALA_CLOUD_API_KEY and STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET were committed to git in HANDOFF.json before the team realized the exposure; required credential rotation
The entire/* branch checkpoint system captures full conversation transcripts including pasted secrets — no scrubbing mechanism exists, rotation is the only mitigation
PR review comments not easily fetchable via REST for bot reviewers (Copilot); had to use GraphQL for thread resolution
merge conflicts in ROADMAP.md and STATE.md required manual resolution after merging main into the phase branch
open_items: CVM epoch key persistence was verified manually during this session — no automated regression test exists for this property; consider adding to the test suite
SSRF probe deduplication: connection-test.ts has similar probe logic to sdk-core — deferred as significant refactor not worth phase 35 churn

String zeroing for auth tokens (migration-worker.ts) is fundamentally ineffective in JS due to string immutability — acknowledged with comment, no real fix possible without changing provider constructor signatures
35-HUMAN-UAT.md persists with status: partial — will surface in /gsd:progress and /gsd:audit-uat until /gsd:verify-work is run against it
Phase 35 directory name 'phala-testnet-tee-migration' is a misnomer (no testnet exists) — docs updated but directory name retained to avoid breaking cross-references
Republish latency baselines (~1155ms avg) are network-bound from remote test machine to Phala Cloud; production co-location latency not yet measured
